chunks: The Commander of the Believers (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, God is Beautiful and loves beauty, and He loves that He sees the effects of His bounty upon His servant.'

key_terms.أَثَرَ النِّعْمَةِ: the effect/trace of bounty — the outward visible expression or mark that God's blessing has been received and used
key_terms.النِّعْمَةِ: ni'ma — divine bounty or blessing; Quranic term for God's gifts to humanity
key_terms.الْجَمَالَ: beauty — used here both as divine attribute and as the quality God loves to see reflected in His creation
key_terms.جَمِيلٌ: Beautiful — one of the divine attributes (asma' al-husna); when applied to God, it signifies transcendent, absolute beauty

ai.seo_question: Does Islam encourage showing outward signs of God's blessings?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted through Imam al-Sadiq from Imam 'Ali (peace be upon both of them), establishes the theological principle that God possesses beauty as an attribute and correspondingly loves beauty in His creation. It further teaches that God loves to witness the visible signs of His blessings upon His servants, implying that expressing and displaying God's bounties is not ostentation but rather a form of divine gratitude. This teaching shaped Islamic ethics around appearance, dress, and the outward expression of God's gifts, encouraging believers to live in a manner that reflects the blessings they have received.
